verdicts.reason: A has no shared left edge: the logo and headline sit at about x=88, the subhead at 70, the pills at 65 and 106, and the legal line at 88. The three flavour pills are split across two staggered rows so they read as scattered pieces, the headline is squeezed into three short lines, and the CTA hangs off to the right with no anchor. B keeps one clean left margin, puts the pills in a single even row, and gives the CTA a clear pairing with the subhead. B's flaws are a large dead gap (about 130px) between the headline and the subhead, a reversed pill order (Honey Rosemary first, Blood Orange last), and legal text that is close to illegibly small.
